name: inprocess-obi-apb-two-ip-i2c-timer-swapped-f1f6
description: The same one-CPU-two-target declaration with the target rows swapped: the PULP I2C is target 0 at 0x40001000 and the PULP timer with its F5 behavior is target 1 at 0x40002000. It exists to show that changing which profile a target index names changes only the declaration: the host source and the loop are not edited, and the F5 handler follows irq_base to the timer's new window.
notes: This is the swapped twin of inprocess-obi-apb-two-ip-timer-i2c-f1f6.json: the two target rows exchange their profiles and windows while the host source, the C++ loop and the generated trait shape stay the same. It is the evidence that target 1 can name another profile without a CPU x IP branch.

Target 1 is the PULP timer with configs/behaviors/pulp_timer_f5.json, so target_for_f5 selects index 1 and build_layout states irq_base = 0x40002000; the F5 firmware and the ISR read at that base rather than at the first target window.
Target 0 is the PULP I2C held at scl/sda = 1. It is reached by address only and declares no F5 facts.
